description: Late Roman enclosure, excavation revealed a 'special' deposit, which was associated with sheep sacrifice, leading the enclosure to be interpreted as some kind of religious focus, and the RSRB to identify it as a shrine. The whole enclosure replaced an earlier farmstead originating in the Iron Age.
bibliography: Luke, M, and T Preece. “Iron Age, Roman and Saxo-Norman Settlement on the Oxford Clay at Luton Road.” Bedfordshire Archaeology 26 (2010).
Martyn, Blick, Brindle, and et al. “Luton Road, Wilstead (Bedfordshire).” The Rural Settlement of Roman Britain: an online resource, 2015. https://doi.org/10.5284/1030449.
